subject: Attribute eager-judge token cost to the triggering node (not pooled on harness-judge-drain)
description:
Today all judging tokens pool on one harness task and are invisible per-node — a real gap for a token-economic product now that judgment is EAGER.

CURRENT: the judge runs as a subagent that claims followup/harness-judge-drain (routes/judge.js:13 HARNESS_JUDGE_DRAIN_KEY). recordUsageOnDone (routes/exec.js:23) writes its usage into overlay.usage_records keyed by THAT task_key. So every eager-judge call's tokens land on the harness-judge-drain bucket, not on the node it judged. The per-task token view (task 6e9b897c-2966-4730-ae2a-5f4512fd0c59/9) therefore shows a task's IMPLEMENTATION cost but NOT the wiring+judging overhead it triggered.

WHY IT MATTERS: eager judgment (task C /16) fires one judge call per new node over its edge-set (up to 10 edges — 5 notes + 5 tasks, TASK_CREATE_FANOUT=5), each carrying A's (/14) ~10-node neighborhood payload (heavier than the old endpoint-only judge). So per-task wiring+judging cost is real and grows with graph activity, but unmeasurable per-task. The product story is token economy — this cost must be attributable.

BUILD:
1. When a judge dispatch is for a specific node (the /judge/next?node=<key> eager path, lib/judge.js buildQueueForNode), attribute that dispatch's token usage to the TRIGGERING NODE (the node whose eagerJudge mark / edge-set was judged), in addition to (or instead of) the pooled harness bucket. Thread the node_key through the usage slice (lib/usage-accounting.js usage_records slice carries task_key today — add a judged_node / attribution key) so analytics can roll up judging cost per node.
2. Keep a pooled total too (harness judging overhead), but expose PER-NODE judging cost so a task's true onboarding cost = implementation + wiring + judging.
3. Surface it where per-task cost is shown (analytics route / the /state tokens field that task 6e9b897c.../9 displays).

CAVEAT: a single judge dispatch may judge a node's whole edge-set (one call, up to 10 edges) — attribute the call to that node (the anchor), not split per-edge. The batch/cursor fallback drain (not node-scoped) can stay pooled on the harness task.

TEST: an eager-judge dispatch for node X records its output_tokens against X (queryable via the per-node usage rollup); a non-node-scoped fallback drain stays on the harness bucket; analytics can report judging-cost-per-task. Pairs with the judge-quality bench so each judged node has both QUALITY and COST.

Files: routes/judge.js (node-scoped dispatch attribution), routes/exec.js recordUsageOnDone, lib/usage-accounting.js, routes/analytics.js.
